newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tobacco options busy, vols down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Tobacco options busy, vols down.

text.p: Options on shares of tobacco companies were active Monday and volatilities were down sharply after Friday's landmark settlement agreement with U.S. states.
In particular, Philip Morris Cos Inc options led the pack, but RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp options also were actively traded, traders said. Both trade on the American Stock Exchange.
"We are seeing a fairly substantial implosion of volatility, especially in the front months, in both Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco," said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners.
On Friday, tobacco companies reached a $368.5 billion settlement with 40 states suing the industry.
The head of one brokerage firm's equity options department said the drop in volatilities was expected since they had been pumped up significantly in anticipation of a settlement.
Schwarz said volatility in the July options for both Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco were down about five points from Friday, and were down one to two points in the middle and long term options.
For both Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco, volatilities in the July series were in the mid-40 region.
Schwarz said volatilities in RJR Nabisco front month options had climbed over 60 before the deal.
"It's a new security as of Friday once the deal was done, and now people are assessing what that security will trade like," he said.
The options department chief said his desk was busy in Philip Morris right up until the settlement announcement Friday afternoon but activity had cooled a bit Monday.
"There's still some interest," he said. "We've had some people come in with some interest in the LEAPS (long-term options)."

Some analysts and investors do not expect the settlement to be completely finalized for six to 12 months, he said, and it could take the companies' stocks that long to reflect the different landscape carved out by the agreement.

"I think you're going to see analysts putting their pencils to it trying to assess exactly what this deal means," Schwarz added. "You're talking about huge amounts of money and taking away a huge cloud of litigation -- assuming it goes through."
Some analysts have already commented on the deal.
Oppenheimer & Co said Monday it raised its price targets and trimmed fiscal 1998 earnings estimates for some tobacco companies including Philip Morris and RJR Nabisco.

Bernie Schaeffer, president of Investment Research Institute in Cincinnati, said in a report he sees "significantly" greater downside potential than upside for Philip Morris, mainly because of a bullish options profile.
In any case, speculation could still remain steady.
"It's still somewhat of a bumpy road as the deal goes through Congress and gets through the lawyers," Schwarz said.
